_why: EVERY ANSWER FOR THE apps.gov.in UPLOAD FORM, EACH WITH ITS EVIDENCE, so the owner types from this file
and never from memory. Text fields are never copied here: a `from` names the listing file beside this
one, which is the single copy (the guards hold those files to the form's limits).
Two checks hold this file. tooling/ci/assert-store-metadata.mjs checks its shape on every run: every
step, the minimum-platform label against the form's own list, `from` naming a real file, eleven
step-3 answers, and the two OWNER FILLS fields. tooling/ci/assert-apps-gov-in-apk.mjs checks it against
the BUILT .apk in CI: the minimum platform must be the .apk's own minSdk, and the five device-permission
answers must agree with the permissions the .apk requests.
The owner fills exactly two fields at the sitting, supportEmail and supportPhone. Both are shown on the
store, and neither is written into this repository.
portalSource: apps.gov.in developer upload form, script /Developer/chunk-ZVEOEZCZ.js and the on-screen lists, read 2026-09-22. Private runbooks/store-submission-apps-gov-in.md 'Step 1' to 'Step 3' and the 2026-09-22 08:20Z corrections.

minimumPlatform.label: Nougat 7.0
minimumPlatform.source: the built .apk's minSdk (Flutter 3.47.5's default flutter.minSdkVersion, 24), read in CI from `aapt2 dump badging` by tooling/ci/assert-apps-gov-in-apk.mjs, which fails if this sdk or label disagrees with the .apk. The label is the form's own name for SDK 24 (contracts/store/vocabulary.js STORE_FORM_RULES['apps-gov-in'].minPlatformLabels).

stateUt.why: The app is not specific to one state or union territory. The form lists an app under the one chosen.

step1._supportWhy: Both are shown on the store. The phone field takes at most 12 characters. Neither is written into this repository.

authorizationLetter.why: The letter's control (financeDocument) is tied to the Finance category. category.txt is Others, so the control does not appear.

applicationType.why: The app talks to its own backend when signed in, and has sign-in (step 3 question 11 is Yes). Private research/session-2026-09-21/prep-apps-gov-in-policy.md section 2.

paymentGateway.why: This channel's purchaseRail is `none` (tooling/channel-register.json apps-gov-in). A build with RELEASE_CHANNEL=apps-gov-in resolves the rail that sells nothing: packages/purchases/test/chassis_billing_test.dart:276, 'a `rail: none` channel is a rail that sells nothing' (BillingRailRefusal.channelSellsNothing).

fileFormat.why: The form takes APK or AAB. With an APK the form asks no key-store question, and the .apk is signed with our own apps.gov.in key.

appFile.why: Built by the Android job of .github/workflows/build-platforms.yml. That artifact name exists only when the signer matches the pin recorded in tooling/channel-register.json apps-gov-in.signing.signingCertificate.sha256. Any other build is named ...-NOT-FOR-UPLOAD-<reason> and must never be uploaded (docs/ci/build-platforms.md).

keyStore.why: The form's script requires the key-store field only when File format is AAB: `if(c=="AAB"){ keyStore.setValidators([required]) }` (Private runbooks/store-submission-apps-gov-in.md, 2026-09-22 08:20Z corrections). The .apk is signed in CI with alias nikatru-appsgovin (tooling/channel-register.json apps-gov-in.signing).
